headline: What keeps me choosing everyone but my soulmate?
note:
FRAME: soulmate x age band. NO MAN EXISTS YET — she asks WHEN or WHETHER. Must not fall through to decode-him, which would have Evelyn invent a man.
🔴 THE AGE BAND LIVES IN THE AD SET, NEVER IN THE COPY. No age, no number, no life-stage, nothing she could check.
🔴 NO DURATION, forward or back. Every frame bans a DATE; this family's own gap was that 'not much longer' is a LENGTH, and a length is not a date. Nothing here gives one.
⚠ SHE is the subject of beats 3-6; the male figure is described in beats 1-2 and retired there.
⚠ NO FAMILY-LINE LANGUAGE anywhere in the read.

🔴 THE AD BLAMES HER CHOOSING OUTRIGHT. Beat 3 declines it three ways — 'your picking was never poor' · 'nothing's off in your judgement' · 'you trusted right'.
⛔ Beat 5 must not turn the block into an enemy placing men in her path — 'never an unnamed enemy, never someone is working against you'. It names a POSITION, not an actor.

readback.1 would a person say this: Yes. 'And it's looked like your doing' is exactly the thought the ad plants.
readback.2 is every noun real: Four objects each with a use, the inverted figure, the mid-step feet — all on the card.
readback.3 anything she could catch me getting wr: No. Beat 4 says nobody has been the one and she has blamed her own choosing. Her ad says both.
readback.4 does the symbol prove the line at a gl: Yes. Four things each with a use proves 'you pick well' without explaining.

a: You turned the Magician. You had no way of knowing, and you took the one with it all laid out.
Look at his table. A cup, a coin, a blade and a wand, out in the open.
You asked what keeps you choosing everyone but your soulmate. It's the open table that stops me — nothing on it is hidden.
And yet it keeps being everyone but the one. You've started to think it comes down to how you pick.
Something turns up each time this gets close to settling. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what has hold of this…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. The backs told you nothing, and you found the calmest face in the deck.
He hangs by one ankle, upside down. Look at his face, though — it's calm.
You asked what keeps you choosing everyone but your soulmate. What I'm reading is the hold itself, and how little of it there is.
Still, it's everyone but the one. And the question keeps landing back on your judgement.
The hold on this is even, and nothing about it slips. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's behind this…
c: You turned the Fool. Nothing marked the backs, and you took the one already on the move.
Look at his feet. One is off the ground, and the other is coming after it.
You asked what keeps you choosing everyone but your soulmate. What I'm looking at is the moment before that step lands.
But it's everyone but the one. And you're still the one asking why.
Something sits where that step comes down, at the front of this. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's sitting there…
